statements.subject: server
statements.description: Layer 1: Canonical Data Model defines the core data structures and message formats that all A2A implementations must understand.
actions: All A2A implementations must understand the core data structures and message formats defined in the canonical data model

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Layer 2: Abstract Operations describes the fundamental capabilities and behaviors that A2A agents must support, independent of how they are exposed over specific protocols.
actions: A2A agents must support the fundamental capabilities and behaviors described in the abstract operations layer regardless of the specific protocol binding used

statements.subject: artifact
statements.description: A generated JSON artifact (spec/a2a.json, produced at build time and not committed) MAY be published for convenience to tooling and the website, but it is a non-normative build artifact.
actions: publish spec/a2a.json for convenience to tooling and the website as a non-normative build artifact

statements.subject: server
statements.description: SDK language bindings, schemas, and any other derived forms MUST be regenerated from the proto (directly or via code generation) rather than edited manually.
actions: regenerate SDK language bindings, schemas, and all derived forms from the proto file
do not edit derived forms manually

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Migration guidance MUST be provided via an ancillary document when introducing major breaking changes.
actions: provide migration guidance via an ancillary document when introducing major breaking changes

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Legacy documentation anchors MUST be preserved (as hidden HTML anchors) to avoid breaking inbound links.
actions: preserve legacy documentation anchors as hidden HTML anchors

statements.subject: server
statements.description: SDKs and JSON Schemas SHOULD provide deprecated alias types/definitions to maintain backward compatibility.
actions: provide deprecated alias types/definitions in SDKs and JSON Schemas to maintain backward compatibility

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A deprecated name SHOULD NOT be removed earlier than the next major version after introduction of its replacement.
actions: retain deprecated names until at least the next major version after introduction of their replacement

statements.subject: server
statements.description: These operations define the fundamental capabilities that all A2A implementations must support, regardless of the underlying binding mechanism.
actions: Support all core A2A operations regardless of the underlying binding mechanism

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Agents SHOULD use this to tailor their output.
actions: Tailor output based on the acceptedOutputModes list provided by the client

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server MUST NOT return more messages than the provided value, but MAY apply a lower limit.
actions: Ensure the number of returned messages does not exceed the historyLength value

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If false (default), the operation MUST wait until the task reaches a terminal (COMPLETED, FAILED, CANCELED, REJECTED) or interrupted (INPUT_REQUIRED, AUTH_REQUIRED) state before returning.
statements.post_cond: task.state = TASK_STATE_COMPLETED | task.state = TASK_STATE_FAILED | task.state = TASK_STATE_CANCELED | task.state = TASK_STATE_REJECTED | task.state = TASK_STATE_INPUT_REQUIRED | task.state = TASK_STATE_AUTH_REQUIRED
actions: Block the operation from returning until the task reaches a terminal or interrupted state

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The operation MUST wait until the task reaches a terminal state (COMPLETED, FAILED, CANCELED, REJECTED) or an interrupted state (INPUT_REQUIRED, AUTH_REQUIRED) before returning.
statements.post_cond: task.state = TASK_STATE_COMPLETED | task.state = TASK_STATE_FAILED | task.state = TASK_STATE_CANCELED | task.state = TASK_STATE_REJECTED | task.state = TASK_STATE_INPUT_REQUIRED | task.state = TASK_STATE_AUTH_REQUIRED
actions: Block the operation from returning until the task reaches a terminal or interrupted state

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The response MUST include the latest task state with all artifacts and status information.
statements.post_cond: response.task.state != null & response.task.artifacts != null & response.task.status != null
actions: Include latest task state in the response
Include all artifacts in the response
Include status information in the response

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The operation MUST return immediately after creating the task, even if processing is still in progress.
actions: Return response immediately after task creation without waiting for task completion

statements.subject: streaming
statements.description: A StreamResponse MUST contain exactly one of the following: task, message, statusUpdate, artifactUpdate
actions: Include exactly one of: task, message, statusUpdate, artifactUpdate in each StreamResponse object

statements.subject: server
statements.description: 0: No history should be returned; the history field SHOULD be omitted
actions: Omit the history field from the response when historyLength is 0

statements.subject: extension
statements.description: Custom protocol bindings MUST specify how service parameters are transmitted in their binding specification.
actions: Document how service parameters are transmitted in the custom protocol binding specification

statements.subject: server
statements.description: As service parameter names MAY need to co-exist with other parameters defined by the underlying transport protocol or infrastructure, all service parameters defined by this specification will be prefixed with a2a-.
actions: Co-exist service parameter names with other parameters defined by the underlying transport protocol or infrastructure

statements.subject: message
statements.description: Send Message operations MAY be idempotent.
actions: Treat duplicate Send Message operations as idempotent, optionally using messageId to detect duplicates

statements.subject: task
statements.description: A duplicate cancellation request MAY return TaskNotFoundError if the task has already been canceled and purged.
actions: Return TaskNotFoundError for duplicate cancellation request

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Servers MUST return appropriate errors and SHOULD provide actionable information to help clients resolve issues.
actions: Return appropriate errors to clients

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Servers MUST reject requests with invalid or missing authentication credentials
actions: Reject the request with an authentication error

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Servers SHOULD include authentication challenge information in the error response
actions: Include authentication challenge information in the error response

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Servers SHOULD specify which authentication scheme is required
actions: Specify which authentication scheme is required in the error response

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Servers MUST return an authorization error when the authenticated client lacks required permissions
actions: Return an authorization error

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Servers SHOULD indicate what permission or scope is missing (without leaking sensitive information about resources the client cannot access)
actions: Indicate the missing permission or scope in the error response without leaking sensitive information about resources the client cannot access

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Servers MUST NOT reveal the existence of resources the client is not authorized to access
actions: Suppress any indication of the existence of resources the client is not authorized to access

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Servers MUST validate all input parameters before processing
actions: Validate all input parameters before processing the request

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Servers SHOULD specify which parameter(s) failed validation and why
actions: Identify which parameter(s) failed validation and provide the reason in the error response

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Servers SHOULD provide guidance on valid parameter values or formats
actions: Provide guidance on valid parameter values or formats in the error response

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Servers MUST return a not found error when a requested resource does not exist or is not accessible to the authenticated client
actions: Return a not found error

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Servers SHOULD NOT distinguish between "does not exist" and "not authorized" to prevent information leakage
actions: Return the same error response for non-existent and unauthorized resources to prevent information leakage

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Servers SHOULD return appropriate error codes for temporary failures vs. permanent errors
actions: Return error codes that distinguish between temporary failures and permanent errors

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Servers MAY include retry guidance (e.g., Retry-After header in HTTP)
actions: Include retry guidance (e.g., Retry-After header in HTTP) in the error response

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Servers SHOULD log system errors for diagnostic purposes
actions: Log system errors for diagnostic purposes

statements.subject: server
statements.description: All error responses in the A2A protocol, regardless of binding, MUST convey the following information:
actions: Include a machine-readable Error Code in the error response
Include a human-readable Error Message in the error response
Optionally include an Error Details array in the error response

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Each object in the array MUST include a @type key that identifies the object's type (using ProtoJSON Any representation).
actions: Include a @type key in each error detail array object that identifies the object's type using ProtoJSON Any representation

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Well-known types from the google.rpc error model (e.g., ErrorInfo, BadRequest) SHOULD be used where applicable.
actions: Use well-known types from the google.rpc error model (e.g., ErrorInfo, BadRequest) in error detail objects where applicable

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Protocol bindings MUST map these elements to their native error representations while preserving semantic meaning.
actions: Map error code, error message, and error details to the native error representation of the protocol binding
Preserve the semantic meaning of all error elements during mapping

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Agents MAY accept additional messages for tasks in non-terminal states to enable multi-turn interactions (see Section 3.4).
statements.pre_cond: task.state != TASK_STATE_COMPLETED & task.state != TASK_STATE_FAILED & task.state != TASK_STATE_CANCELED
actions: Accept additional messages for tasks in non-terminal states to support multi-turn interactions

statements.subject: server
statements.description: When clients attempt to use operations or features that require capabilities not declared as supported in the Agent Card, the agent MUST return an appropriate error response:
actions: Return an appropriate error response indicating the capability is not supported

statements.subject: push_notification
statements.description: If AgentCard.capabilities.pushNotifications is false or not present, operations related to push notification configuration (Create, Get, List, Delete) MUST return PushNotificationNotSupportedError.
actions: Return PushNotificationNotSupportedError

statements.subject: streaming
statements.description: If AgentCard.capabilities.streaming is false or not present, attempts to use SendStreamingMessage or SubscribeToTask operations MUST return UnsupportedOperationError.
actions: Return UnsupportedOperationError for SendStreamingMessage or SubscribeToTask operations

statements.subject: agent_card
statements.description: If AgentCard.capabilities.extendedAgentCard is false or not present, attempts to call the Get Extended Agent Card operation MUST return UnsupportedOperationError.
actions: Return UnsupportedOperationError

statements.subject: agent_card
statements.description: If the agent declares support but has not configured an extended card, it MUST return ExtendedAgentCardNotConfiguredError.
actions: Return ExtendedAgentCardNotConfiguredError

statements.subject: extension
statements.description: When a server requests use of an extension marked as required: true in the Agent Card but the client does not declare support for it, the agent MUST return ExtensionSupportRequiredError.
actions: Return ExtensionSupportRequiredError

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Clients SHOULD validate capability support by examining the Agent Card before attempting operations that require optional capabilities.
actions: Examine the Agent Card to validate that required optional capabilities are declared before attempting the operation

statements.subject: context
statements.description: Agents MAY generate a new contextId when processing a Message that does not include a contextId field
actions: Generate a new contextId

statements.subject: context
statements.description: If an agent generates a new contextId, it MUST be included in the response (either Task or Message)
actions: Include generated contextId in response (Task or Message)

statements.subject: context
statements.description: Agents MAY accept and preserve client-provided contextId values
actions: Accept client-provided contextId
Preserve client-provided contextId value

statements.subject: context
statements.description: If an agent cannot accept a client-provided contextId, it MUST reject the request with an error and MUST NOT generate a new contextId for the response
actions: Reject the request with an error

statements.subject: context
statements.description: Clients SHOULD NOT provide a client-generated contextId to a server unless they understand how the server will process that contextId
actions: Do not provide a client-generated contextId to a server when server contextId processing behavior is not understood

statements.subject: context
statements.description: Server-generated contextId values SHOULD be treated as opaque identifiers by clients
actions: Treat server-generated contextId values as opaque identifiers

statements.subject: context
statements.description: All tasks and messages with the same contextId SHOULD be treated as part of the same conversational session
actions: Treat all tasks and messages with the same contextId as part of the same conversational session

statements.subject: context
statements.description: Agents MAY use the contextId to maintain internal state, conversational history, or LLM context across multiple interactions
actions: Use contextId to maintain internal state
Use contextId to maintain conversational history
Use contextId to maintain LLM context across multiple interactions

statements.subject: context
statements.description: Agents MAY implement context expiration or cleanup policies and SHOULD document any such policies
actions: Implement context expiration or cleanup policies

statements.subject: task
statements.description: Agents MUST generate a unique taskId for each new task they create
actions: Generate a unique taskId for each new task created

statements.subject: task
statements.description: The generated taskId MUST be included in the Task object returned to the client
actions: Include generated taskId in the Task object returned to the client

statements.subject: task
statements.description: When a client includes a taskId in a Message, it MUST reference an existing task
actions: Reference an existing task when including taskId in a Message

statements.subject: task
statements.description: Agents MUST return a TaskNotFoundError if the provided taskId does not correspond to an existing task
actions: Return a TaskNotFoundError to the client

statements.subject: context
statements.description: Clients MAY include the contextId in subsequent messages to indicate continuation of a previous interaction
actions: Include contextId in subsequent messages to indicate continuation of a previous interaction

statements.subject: task
statements.description: Clients MAY use taskId (with or without contextId) to continue or refine a specific task
actions: Use taskId to continue or refine a specific task

statements.subject: context
statements.description: Clients MAY use contextId without taskId to start a new task within an existing conversation context
actions: Use contextId without taskId to start a new task within an existing conversation context

statements.subject: context
statements.description: Agents MUST infer contextId from the task if only taskId is provided
actions: Infer contextId from the referenced task when only taskId is provided in the message

statements.subject: message
statements.description: Agents MUST reject messages containing mismatching contextId and taskId (i.e., the provided contextId is different from that of the referenced Task).
statements.pre_cond: message.contextId != null & message.taskId != null & message.contextId != task.contextId
actions: Reject the message containing mismatching contextId and taskId

statements.subject: message
statements.description: Clients SHOULD use the referenceTaskIds field in Message to explicitly reference related tasks
actions: Populate the referenceTaskIds field in Message to explicitly reference related tasks

statements.subject: task
statements.description: Agents SHOULD use referenced tasks to understand the context and intent of follow-up requests
actions: Use referenced tasks to understand the context and intent of follow-up requests

statements.subject: context
statements.description: Agents SHOULD leverage the shared contextId to provide contextually relevant responses
actions: Leverage shared contextId to provide contextually relevant responses

statements.subject: streaming
statements.description: All implementations MUST deliver events in the order they were generated.
actions: Deliver events to clients in the order they were generated

statements.subject: streaming
statements.description: Events MUST NOT be reordered during transmission, regardless of protocol binding.
actions: Preserve event order during transmission regardless of which protocol binding is used

statements.subject: server
statements.description: An agent MAY serve multiple concurrent streams to one or more clients for the same task.
actions: Serve multiple concurrent streams to one or more clients for the same task

statements.subject: streaming
statements.description: Events MUST be broadcast to all active streams for that task
actions: Broadcast each generated event to all currently active streams for that task

statements.subject: streaming
statements.description: Each stream MUST receive the same events in the same order
actions: Deliver the same set of events to each active stream
Deliver those events in the same order to each active stream

statements.subject: streaming
statements.description: Closing one stream MUST NOT affect other active streams for the same task
actions: Leave all other active streams for the same task unaffected when one stream is closed

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Patch version numbers SHOULD NOT be used in requests, responses and Agent Cards, and MUST not be considered when clients and servers negotiate protocol versions.
statements.post_cond: request.version_format = Major.Minor & response.version_format = Major.Minor & agent_card.version_format = Major.Minor
actions: Omit patch version numbers from requests
Omit patch version numbers from responses
Omit patch version numbers from Agent Cards

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Clients MUST send the A2A-Version header with each request to maintain compatibility after an agent upgrades to a new version of the protocol (except for 0.3 Clients - 0.3 will be assumed for empty header).
actions: Include A2A-Version header in each request sent to the agent

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Clients MAY provide the A2A-Version as a request parameter instead of a header.
actions: Include A2A-Version as a query/request parameter instead of an HTTP header

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Agents MUST process requests using the semantics of the requested A2A-Version (matching Major.Minor).
actions: Process the request using the semantics of the A2A-Version specified in the request, matching Major.Minor

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the version is not supported by the interface, agents MUST return a VersionNotSupportedError.
actions: Return a VersionNotSupportedError response to the client

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Agents MUST interpret empty value as 0.3 version.
actions: Interpret an empty A2A-Version header value as protocol version 0.3

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Tooling libraries and SDKs that implement the A2A protocol MUST provide mechanisms to help clients manage protocol versioning, such as negotiation of the transport and protocol version used.
actions: Provide mechanisms to help clients manage protocol versioning
Support negotiation of the transport and protocol version used

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Client Agents that require the latest features of the protocol should be configured to request specific versions and avoid automatic fallback to older versions, to prevent silently losing functionality.
actions: Configure client to request specific protocol versions
Disable automatic fallback to older protocol versions

statements.subject: message
statements.description: Messages SHOULD NOT be used to deliver task outputs.
actions: Do not use Messages to deliver task outputs

statements.subject: artifact
statements.description: Results SHOULD BE returned using Artifacts associated with a Task.
actions: Return task results using Artifacts associated with the Task

statements.subject: streaming
statements.description: Clients using streaming to retrieve task updates MAY not receive all status update messages if the client is disconnected and then reconnects.
actions: Client may not receive all status update messages missed during disconnection period

statements.subject: message
statements.description: Messages MUST NOT be considered a reliable delivery mechanism for critical information.
actions: Do not treat Messages as a reliable delivery mechanism for critical information

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Agents MAY choose to persist all Messages that contain important information in the Task history to ensure clients can retrieve it later.
actions: Persist all Messages containing important information in Task history
Make persisted Messages available for later client retrieval

statements.subject: client
statements.description: However, clients MUST NOT rely on this behavior unless negotiated out-of-band.
actions: Do not assume agents will persist all Messages unless explicitly negotiated out-of-band

statements.subject: server
statements.description: All protocol bindings MUST provide functionally equivalent representations of these data structures.
actions: provide functionally equivalent representations of the Protocol Buffers canonical data structures for all protocol bindings

statements.subject: message
statements.description: For server messages, context_id must be provided, and task_id only if a task was created.
actions: Set context_id on all server-originated messages
Set task_id only if a task was created in association with this message

statements.subject: message
statements.description: For client messages, both fields are optional, with the caveat that if both are provided, they have to match (the context_id has to be the one that is set on the task).
actions: Treat contextId and taskId as optional on client messages
If both contextId and taskId are provided, verify contextId matches the contextId set on the referenced task

statements.subject: part
statements.description: Note: A Part MUST contain exactly one of the following: text, raw, url, data
actions: Ensure each Part contains exactly one content field from the set: text, raw, url, data

statements.subject: artifact
statements.description: It must be unique within a task.
actions: Assign an artifactId that is unique within the scope of its containing task

statements.subject: artifact
statements.description: Must contain at least one part.
actions: Ensure the artifact's parts array contains at least one Part element

statements.subject: push_notification
statements.description: The agent MUST include authentication credentials in the request headers as specified in the PushNotificationConfig.authentication field.
actions: Include authentication credentials in the HTTP request headers as specified in PushNotificationConfig.authentication

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Clients MUST respond with HTTP 2xx status codes to acknowledge successful receipt
actions: Respond with HTTP 2xx status code to acknowledge successful receipt of the push notification

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Clients SHOULD process notifications idempotently, as duplicate deliveries may occur
actions: Process push notifications idempotently to handle duplicate deliveries safely

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Clients MUST validate the task ID matches an expected task
actions: Validate that the task ID in the push notification payload matches an expected task

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Clients SHOULD implement appropriate security measures to verify the notification source
actions: Implement appropriate security measures to verify the source of the push notification

statements.subject: push_notification
statements.description: Agents MUST attempt delivery at least once for each configured webhook
actions: Attempt HTTP POST delivery to each configured webhook URL at least once when a task update occurs

statements.subject: push_notification
statements.description: Agents MAY implement retry logic with exponential backoff for failed deliveries
actions: Implement retry logic with exponential backoff upon failed webhook delivery

statements.subject: push_notification
statements.description: Agents SHOULD include a reasonable timeout for webhook requests (recommended: 10-30 seconds)
actions: Set a reasonable timeout (recommended 10-30 seconds) on outgoing webhook HTTP POST requests

statements.subject: push_notification
statements.description: Agents MAY stop attempting delivery after a configured number of consecutive failures
actions: Cease further delivery attempts after a configured number of consecutive webhook delivery failures

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If true, the client must understand and comply with the extension's requirements.
actions: Understand the extension's requirements
Comply with the extension's requirements

statements.subject: agent_card
statements.description: Must be a valid absolute HTTPS URL in production.
actions: Set the AgentInterface url field to a valid absolute HTTPS URL

statements.subject: agent_card
statements.description: A SecurityScheme MUST contain exactly one of the following: apiKeySecurityScheme, httpAuthSecurityScheme, oauth2SecurityScheme, openIdConnectSecurityScheme, mtlsSecurityScheme
actions: Ensure SecurityScheme object contains exactly one of: apiKeySecurityScheme, httpAuthSecurityScheme, oauth2SecurityScheme, openIdConnectSecurityScheme, mtlsSecurityScheme

statements.subject: agent_card
statements.description: This value should be registered in the IANA Authentication Scheme registry.
actions: Register the HTTP authentication scheme value in the IANA Authentication Scheme registry

statements.subject: agent_card
statements.description: TLS is required.
actions: Serve the OAuth2 authorization server metadata URL exclusively over TLS

statements.subject: agent_card
statements.description: A OAuthFlows MUST contain exactly one of the following: authorizationCode, clientCredentials, implicit, password, deviceCode
actions: Ensure OAuthFlows object contains exactly one of: authorizationCode, clientCredentials, implicit, password, deviceCode

statements.subject: client
statements.description: PKCE should always be used for public clients and is recommended for all clients.
actions: Always use PKCE (RFC 7636) when the client is a public client performing the Authorization Code flow
Use PKCE (RFC 7636) for all clients performing the Authorization Code flow

statements.subject: extension
statements.description: Extensions SHOULD include version information in their URI identifier.
actions: Include version information in the extension's URI identifier

statements.subject: extension
statements.description: A new URI MUST be created for breaking changes to an extension.
actions: Create a new URI for the extension when introducing breaking changes

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If a client requests a versions of an extension that the agent does not support, the agent SHOULD ignore the extension for that interaction and proceed without it, unless the extension is marked as required in the AgentCard, in which case the agent MUST return an error indicating unsupported extension.
statements.pre_cond: client.requested_extension = true & server.supports_extension = false & extension.required = false
actions: Ignore the unsupported extension for the interaction
Proceed with the interaction without the extension

statements.subject: server
statements.description: It MUST NOT fall back to a previous version of the extension automatically.
actions: Do not automatically fall back to a previous version of the unsupported extension

statements.subject: server
statements.description: When an agent supports multiple protocols, all supported protocols MUST: Provide the same set of operations and capabilities; Return semantically equivalent results for the same requests; Map errors consistently using appropriate protocol-specific codes; Support the same authentication schemes declared in the AgentCard
statements.post_cond: agent.protocols.functionality = equivalent & agent.protocols.behavior = equivalent & agent.protocols.error_handling = consistent & agent.protocols.authentication_schemes = equivalent
actions: Provide the same set of operations and capabilities across all supported protocols
Return semantically equivalent results for the same requests across all supported protocols
Map errors consistently using appropriate protocol-specific codes across all supported protocols
Support the same authentication schemes declared in the AgentCard across all supported protocols

statements.subject: agent_card
statements.description: Agents MUST declare all supported protocols in their AgentCard
actions: Declare all supported protocols in the AgentCard

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Clients MAY choose any protocol declared by the agent
actions: Select any protocol from the set of protocols declared in the agent's AgentCard

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Clients SHOULD implement fallback logic for alternative protocols
actions: Implement fallback logic that attempts alternative protocols when the primary protocol is unavailable or fails

statements.subject: server
statements.description: All A2A-specific errors defined in Section 3.3.2 MUST be mapped to binding-specific error representations.
actions: Map every A2A-specific error type defined in Section 3.3.2 to its corresponding binding-specific error representation

statements.subject: extension
statements.description: Custom protocol bindings MUST define equivalent error code mappings that preserve the semantic meaning of each A2A error type.
actions: Define error code mappings for every A2A error type in the custom binding
Ensure each mapping preserves the semantic meaning of the corresponding A2A error type

statements.subject: extension
statements.description: The binding specification SHOULD provide a similar mapping table showing how each A2A error type is represented in the custom binding's native error format.
actions: Include a mapping table in the binding specification that shows each A2A error type and its representation in the custom binding's native error format

statements.subject: message
statements.description: All JSON serializations of the A2A protocol data model MUST use camelCase naming for field names, not the snake_case convention used in Protocol Buffer definitions.
actions: Use camelCase naming for all JSON field names in A2A protocol data model serializations
Do not use snake_case naming convention for JSON field names

statements.subject: message
statements.description: Enum values MUST be represented according to the ProtoJSON specification, which serializes enums as their string names as defined in the Protocol Buffer definition (typically SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE).
actions: Serialize enum values as their string names as defined in the Protocol Buffer definition
Use SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE string representation for enum values in JSON

statements.subject: message
statements.description: When serialized to JSON (in JSON-RPC, HTTP/REST, or other JSON-based bindings), these timestamps MUST be represented as ISO 8601 formatted strings in UTC timezone.
actions: Represent timestamps as ISO 8601 formatted strings in UTC timezone

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Precision: Millisecond precision SHOULD be used where available
actions: Use millisecond precision for timestamp fields where available

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Clients and servers MUST parse and generate ISO 8601 timestamps correctly
actions: Parse ISO 8601 timestamps correctly
Generate ISO 8601 timestamps correctly

statements.subject: message
statements.description: When millisecond precision is not available, the fractional seconds portion MAY be omitted or zero-filled
actions: Omit or zero-fill the fractional seconds portion of the timestamp

statements.subject: message
statements.description: Timestamps MUST NOT include timezone offsets other than 'Z' (all times are UTC)
actions: Reject or prohibit timezone offsets other than 'Z' in all timestamps
Ensure all timestamps express UTC using the 'Z' suffix exclusively

statements.subject: message
statements.description: Fields marked with [(google.api.field_behavior) = REQUIRED] indicate that the field MUST be present and set in valid messages.
actions: Ensure the field is present and set in any valid message

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Implementations SHOULD validate these requirements and reject messages with missing required fields.
actions: Validate that all required fields are present in the received message
Reject messages that have missing required fields

statements.subject: message
statements.description: Arrays marked as required MUST contain at least one element.
actions: Ensure that any array field marked as required contains at least one element

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Implementations SHOULD ignore unrecognized fields in messages, allowing for forward compatibility as the protocol evolves.
actions: Ignore any unrecognized fields present in a received message

statements.subject: extension
statements.description: Custom protocol bindings SHOULD be identified by a URI.
actions: Identify the custom protocol binding using a URI

statements.subject: agent_card
statements.description: The protocolBinding field in the Agent Card's supportedInterfaces entry SHOULD be a URI:
actions: Set the protocolBinding field in the Agent Card's supportedInterfaces entry to a URI value

statements.subject: extension
statements.description: When a breaking change is introduced to a binding, a new URI MUST be used so that clients can distinguish between incompatible versions:
actions: Assign a new URI to the updated binding
Ensure the new URI is distinct from all prior incompatible versions of the binding

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Production deployments MUST use encrypted communication (HTTPS for HTTP-based bindings, TLS for gRPC).
actions: Use HTTPS for HTTP-based transport bindings
Use TLS for gRPC transport bindings

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Implementations SHOULD use modern TLS configurations (TLS 1.3+ recommended) with strong cipher suites.
actions: Configure TLS 1.3 or higher
Use strong cipher suites in TLS configuration

statements.subject: client
statements.description: A2A Clients SHOULD verify the A2A Server's identity by validating its TLS certificate against trusted certificate authorities (CAs) during the TLS handshake.
actions: Validate the A2A Server's TLS certificate against trusted certificate authorities (CAs)

statements.subject: server
statements.description: MUST authenticate every incoming request based on the provided credentials and its declared authentication requirements.
actions: Authenticate every incoming request using the provided credentials
Enforce declared authentication requirements for every request

statements.subject: server
statements.description: SHOULD use appropriate binding-specific error codes for authentication challenges or rejections.
actions: Return a binding-specific error code appropriate for the authentication challenge or rejection

statements.subject: server
statements.description: SHOULD provide relevant authentication challenge information with error responses.
actions: Include relevant authentication challenge information in the error response

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Authorization logic is implementation-specific and MAY consider: Specific skills requested, Actions attempted within tasks, Data access policies, OAuth scopes (if applicable)
actions: Evaluate requested skills against authorization policy
Evaluate actions attempted within tasks against authorization policy
Evaluate data access policies
Evaluate OAuth scopes if applicable

statements.subject: server
